note: Judged against the criteria as stated, not against his enthusiasm. MISSES: 'successful' — he works two hourly jobs, county environmental field work by day and restaurant serving by night, which is not the business-owner-or-physician profile the ICP names. 'Neglected_health' — the criterion explicitly means health is the neglected area, NOT a crisis; his is a crisis, with four concurrently medicated conditions, a deferred knee surgery, a colonoscopy the following week and five years of unintended weight loss. 'Good_to_great' — this is rescue by any reading; he has done no training for six months under medical instruction and wants to get off his medications and 'just be me again'. MATCHES: 'income' holds better than the occupation would suggest — $4,000 monthly surplus after bills, an 800 credit score, an investment portfolio and a financial advisor; means are not the constraint, allocation is. 'Not_deconditioned' also holds — he is a committed long-term gym-goer who lifted heavy until six months ago, loves training and had already restarted kettlebell work on his own, so he is the opposite of the excluded gym-averse profile. Scored 'outside' because three of five criteria fail, including both of the ones about starting point and severity. Two things follow. First, this reinforces the existing observation that the buying population is wider than the stated ICP — the person the criteria describe and the person on this call share almost nothing except the willingness to pay. Second, and more importantly, it reinforces the observation that the stated ICP has NO clinical criterion: nothing in 'successful / income / neglected_health / good_to_great / not_deconditioned' would have stopped this sale, and the one thing that should have gated it — a physician's standing instruction not to lift heavy weights — is not a criterion at all.
